params.script_inline:
import sys, json

d = json.load(sys.stdin)
header = d.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}
msgs = d.get("messages", [])
calls = [m for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]
results = [m for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_result"]


def emit(out):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)


# --- call pass -------------------------------------------------------------
# The call travels verbatim AND rides along as hop.call (the turn as JSON).
# The wiring's call edge promotes it into context ("call": "hop.call") -- the
# only place a stateless cell can keep it across the tool hop.
if len(calls) == 1:
    turn = calls[0]
    emit([{"header": {"route": "call", "call": json.dumps(turn),
                      "tool_call_id": str(turn.get("id") or "")},
           "messages": [turn]}])

if len(calls) > 1:
    # This unit retries ONE call; bundles are the dispatcher's job. Refuse
    # loudly with every id answered, instead of parking an ambiguous call
    # that a later retry could not rebuild.
    note = "retry unit takes one call per message; put a dispatcher in front"
    emit([{"header": {"route": "error", "error_code": "bundle_not_supported"},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                         "id": str(c.get("id") or ""), "text": note}
                        for c in calls]}])

# --- reply pass ------------------------------------------------------------
error_code = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
if error_code:
    turn = None
    parked = ctx.get("call")
    if isinstance(parked, str):
        try:
            t = json.loads(parked)
            if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("type") == "tool_call":
                turn = t
        except Exception:
            pass
    if turn is not None:
        # The ORIGINAL call re-enters the tool. Whether it MAY is the retry
        # edge's decision (int(context.attempt) < RETRY_MAX) -- this cell
        # neither reads nor writes the counter.
        emit([{"header": {"route": "retry", "error_code": error_code,
                          "tool_call_id": str(turn.get("id") or "")},
               "messages": [turn]}])
    # No (or no rebuildable) parked call: a retry is impossible. Hand the
    # error over as-is instead of looping garbage into the tool.
    emit([{"header": {"route": "error", "error_code": error_code},
           "messages": msgs}])

if results:
    emit([{"header": {"route": "ok",
                      "tool_call_id": str(results[0].get("id") or "")},
           "messages": msgs}])

# Neither a call nor a reply: terminal (empty multi-send by design).
emit([])

retry_max.description: Retry budget (RETRY_MAX): how many times a failed call re-enters the tool before the give-up lane fires. The knob lives in the WIRING, not in this cell -- the retry edge's condition (int(context.attempt) < ${RETRY_MAX:-3}) bounds the loop and its modifier counts (set_context attempt = int(context.attempt) + 1). The cell neither reads nor writes the counter.

description.purpose: Retry router around ONE tool: routes a call towards the tool, watches the reply, and re-emits the ORIGINAL call on an error reply -- bounded by the wiring's retry edge, never by the cell. At the cap the give-up lane hands the last error to an error sink with the original error_code intact.
description.use_when: Between a caller and a tool cell whose failures are worth a bounded second try (network tools, busy stores). Wire five lanes in the SAME mutation that instantiates it: call (parks the call in context and seeds the counter), the tool's reply lane back in, retry (counts and bounds), ok, and the give-up lane onto the error sink.
description.not_in_scope: No counting (context.attempt is written only by the retry edge), no backoff timing (a routing hop is the delay; a real timer belongs to a timer cell), no bundles (one call per message -- put a dispatcher in front), no state, no cell.db, no knowledge of which cell the tool is.
description.emits_meaning: route 'call': the call verbatim towards the tool; hop.call carries the turn as JSON so the call edge can park it (set_context call = hop.call). route 'retry': the ORIGINAL call rebuilt from context.call, hop.error_code says why; the retry edge decides whether it re-enters the tool. route 'ok': the successful tool_result, passed through. route 'error': the terminal lane -- an error with no rebuildable parked call, or a refused bundle (error_code bundle_not_supported, one synthetic tool_result per id). A turn that is neither a call nor a reply emits NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal).
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: either ONE tool_call turn (the call pass) or the tool's reply turns (the reply pass). hop.error_code: set on the reply pass marks the reply as failed -- store/bash/code error replies carry it. context.call: the parked call, written by the wiring's call edge, read to rebuild the retry.
examples: call {id: c1} -> route 'call' with hop.call parked; tool fails (hop.error_code io_error) -> route 'retry' rebuilds c1; retry edge attempt 0 -> 1; tool succeeds -> route 'ok'
tool fails forever, RETRY_MAX 3: attempts 0..3, then the give-up edge hands the LAST error reply to the sink with hop {route: 'error', error_code: io_error, attempt: 3}
a two-call bundle -> route 'error', error_code bundle_not_supported, both ids answered
